title: Offline modprobe hook integration and CRI registry consistency check for airgap bootstrap
author: Meera Patel
release_notes: Adds an opt-in offline kernel-module preloader for air-gapped clusters and improves CRI registry index consistency checks during offline registry seeding. Includes Terraform helper to seed OCI mirror indexes and Helm initContainer changes to ensure modules are present before runtime containers start.
description:
Motivation: Customers deploying Redwood.Private into heavily restricted on-prem or air-gapped environments reported two recurring failure modes during bootstrap: (1) missing kernel modules required by CNI/cri that are not available until after first-boot package sync, causing kubelet/cri to crash-loop; (2) race conditions and checksum mismatches between local OCI mirror state and the installer's CRI registry index leading to opaque image pull failures. This PR introduces a deterministic approach to preload kernel modules during offline bootstrapping and a registry index consistency verifier to make registry seeding and upgrade/rollback operations predictable in air-gapped installs.

Summary of changes (high level): - installer/pkg/bootstrap: add offline-modprobe preloader that reads a distro-agnostic manifest (modules.yaml) shipped in the sealed bundle; it maps modules to vendor-provided tarballs and invokes a privileged init step that extracts and insmod/signed-modprobe checks before the node joins the cluster. The preloader is idempotent and supports dry-run. - installer/helm/redwood-core: introduce an initContainer pattern for daemonset-managed components to wait for a modprobe-ready file in /var/lib/redwood/preloaded-mods; the initContainer will also emit metrics to the console for observability. - tools/registry-seed/terraform: add a terraform helper module (oci_mirror_seed) that computes and write-locks a CRI registry index and generates a signed index bundle consumed by the installer. The module includes checksum and manifest signing steps to avoid silent divergence. - installer/cli: new command `bundle verify-index` which validates the on-disk signed index and provides remediation hints if mismatches are found. - e2e: extend airgap acceptance tests to include a scenario that intentionally corrupts a single-layer blob to validate failure modes and subsequent automatic repair via index reconcile.

Checklist: - [x] Implement offline-modprobe preloader and manifest format - [x] Helm chart changes with initContainer and liveness probes - [x] Terraform module for seeding and signing index - [x] CLI verification command and helpful error messages - [x] Unit tests for manifest parsing and idempotence - [x] Integration tests exercising corrupted-index recovery - [x] Docs update (installer/README) and sample modules.yaml

Commits: ["feat(bootstrap): add offline modprobe preloader (Meera Patel)", "chore(helm): initContainer for preloaded-mods gating (Jared Smith)", "feat(terraform): oci_mirror_seed module with index signer (Ravi Gupta)", "test(e2e): corrupt-blob recovery scenario and reconcile flow (Ana Ortiz)"]

Files changed (representative): ["installer/pkg/bootstrap/preloader.go", "installer/assets/modules.yaml", "installer/cli/verify_index.go", "installer/helm/redwood-core/daemonset.yaml (initContainer addition)", "tools/terraform/modules/oci_mirror_seed/main.tf", "tools/registry-seed/verify_index.sh", "tests/e2e/airgap_corrupt_blob_test.go", "docs/installer/airgap-kernel-modules.md"] Note: preloader.go is ~400 lines (mostly parsing and distro shims); the manifest is intentionally small and extensible.

Review conversation (high level): - Jared Smith (reviewer): "This approach is sensible but needs a stricter rollback path if modprobe fails on older kernels (we should not block node registration forever). Can we make gating configurable with a soft-fail timeout?" - Meera (author): "Added a soft-fail timeout flag and a --strict-modprobe boolean for enterprise installs; documented behavior and added metrics so SREs can see stuck nodes." - Ravi Gupta: "Terraform index signer looks good; can we include an option to seed multiple registries and produce a composite index?" - Meera: "Added composite-index support and tests; default remains single-registry for simplicity." - Ana Ortiz (approver): "Integration tests exercise the recovery flow; observed a flaky e2e on the first run which passed on rerun. Approving."

CI: Initial CI run failed the flaky e2e (timeout on corrupted-blob retry). Triggered rerun of e2e job; second run passed. Lint and unit tests green. Package signing job validated the signed index bundles.

Upgrade and rollback notes: - Upgrades: installer will detect existing preloaded-mods state and will only add new module tarballs; preloader is safe to run on upgrades since checksums are compared and only missing modules are installed. - Rollbacks: new rollback hook in helm chart will attempt to remove modules introduced in the failed release if --strict-modprobe was used; otherwise modules persist (safe). The Terraform seeding module writes a lockfile (oci-index.lock) to the mirror that is used by installer for determinism; rollback of mirrored registry requires mirror operator to apply the lockfile revert.

Security and signing: The registry index and modules manifest are signed using the bundle signing key (existing key material in sealed-bundles). The preloader verifies signatures before any module is insmod'd. We added a defensive path to fail safe (log + skip) for unsigned optional modules with an explicit audit event.

Why this is different from previous work: Prior PRs focused on general offline image bundling and pre-seeding registries. This PR targets the specific bootstrap-time kernel dependency gap and the subtle race where registry indexing and mirror state diverge after network outages or partial seeding. By combining a small, verifiable module manifest with a signed index and a Terraform-friendly seeder we make airgap bootstraps reproducible and debuggable.

Follow-ups (tracked): - ENG-3470: populate distro-specific module tarballs in vendor registry (blocking for some customers) - ENG-3505: automated module ABI compatibility scanner - SRE-118: dashboard for preloader metrics and cluster-level gating alerts.

Merge: Squashed and merged to main after approvals. Changelog and docs updated in the same commit to keep bundle parity.

notes_for_ops: Operators should run the terraform oci_mirror_seed with --write-lock before installing a sealed bundle. If a cluster fails to boot due to missing modules, run `redwood-installer bundle verify-index` to confirm index parity and then `redwood-installer preload --dry-run` to preview changes. If kernel ABI mismatches occur, use the bundle with prebuilt distro-specific tarballs referenced in ENG-3470.
test_plan: Unit tests for manifest parsing and idempotence; integration e2e that corrupts a blob and asserts the reconcile path repairs the mirror and continues bootstrap; manual verification on CentOS7, Ubuntu20.04 and Rocky8 in our internal lab. All tests were green on rerun.
observability: Added two new metrics: redwood.bootstrap.preload.duration_seconds and redwood.bootstrap.preload.failures_total. Installer emits events to audit log when unsigned optional modules are skipped.
documentation_updates: docs/installer/airgap-kernel-modules.md contains module manifest schema, terraform usage example, and troubleshooting steps. README updated with upgrade/rollback notes.
